causes.text: On Jan. 30, 2024, Universal Music Group (UMG) accused TikTok of bullying and said it would remove its catalog from the platform after failing to agree on fair compensation for artists.

source_info.title: Universal Music Group threatens to pull song catalog from TikTok in furious open letter

effects.text: After UMG's songs disappeared from TikTok, many listeners turned to licensed platforms. By the fourth quarter of 2024, Spotify reported that monthly active users climbed 12% to 675 million, and premium subscribers grew to 263 million, exceeding its forecasts.

source_info.title: Spotify Reports Fourth Quarter 2024 Results: User Growth Soars

causal_reasoning_chain.description: Universal Music Group, representing artists like Taylor Swift and Billie Eilish, threatened to pull its entire catalog from TikTok after accusing the platform of offering unfair compensation and allowing unlicensed AI-generated content.

The removal of major artists from TikTok reduced the platform's attractiveness for music discovery. Fans searching for licensed music migrated to subscription services where UMG's catalog remained available.

By late 2024, Spotify's monthly active users had surged 12% to 675 million and premium subscribers increased to 263 million, beating forecasts. The influx of listeners, partly attributable to TikTok's music shortage, helped lift Spotify's stock by roughly 8% over the following months.

rationale: UMG's withdrawal of music from TikTok deprived users of popular songs on the short-video platform. Many fans turned to Spotify and other licensed services to access these tracks, contributing to Spotify's strong user growth in late 2024.
counterfactual_analysis: If UMG had maintained its catalog on TikTok, music fans might have continued discovering songs on TikTok instead of migrating to Spotify, resulting in slower user growth for Spotify.

adversarial_confounders.impact: Aggressive promotions and new features may have boosted user numbers independent of TikTok's issues.

details.pestel_factor: Economic - Regulatory and technology driven forces
details.commentary: Universal Music Group's dispute with TikTok over artist pay and AI-generated content reflected rising legal and social pressure to protect creators on digital platforms. As TikTok lost licensed tracks from major stars, those external pressures pushed more listeners toward fully licensed streaming services such as Spotify.

When UMG removed its catalog from TikTok, some users shifted their music discovery and listening to Spotify, lifting engagement and subscriber growth. Improved user metrics and revenues strengthened investor confidence, allowing Spotify to reinvest in content and product features, which in turn reinforced the platform's growth momentum.
